reason: the red-team lens's findings the code or a test must fix

findings.text: red-team lens, medium: The variable `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE` is exported but never unset or explicitly reset on the fresh-start path, so any parent process that has `_ZBUILD_RESUME_ACTIVE=true` in its environment causes the cycle orchestrator to enter resume-mode behavior (`_is_resume=true`, `_cid_resume_first_iter=true`) on a brand-new run, violating GUAR-1. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:2924; fix: code)

red-team lens, medium: The CMBR-1 `stage.start` emission fires for EVERY non-complete cycle member in the first resumed iteration, not only the interrupted one; members K+1…N (which never ran in this iteration and are dispatched normally) each receive a spurious `stage.start` event that is absent from a fresh run, contradicting the comment at lines 1460-1463 which claims 'Fresh runs and later resumed iterations receive no stage.start for cycle members via this path'. (core/pipeline/cycle-orchestrator.sh:1459; fix: code)

red-team lens, medium: The `cycle:*` arm of the dispatch-unit loop skips a complete cycle with no stale-artifact check, while the `stage:*` arm at line 3792 explicitly verifies the primary artifact is present and exits 1 if absent; a complete cycle whose rehydrated member artifacts are missing silently passes the skip guard rather than failing closed as RHYD-2 requires. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:3502; fix: code)

red-team lens, medium: `_runner_resume_rehydrate` returns 0 (not 1) when `_artifact_persist_restore` fails, delegating the RHYD-2 fail-closed check to the dispatch loop; for `--resume --from-stage`, `_runner_from_stage_preflight` is then called at line 3011 and ALSO calls `_artifact_persist_restore`+`_artifact_persist_put_back`, causing two git state-branch checkouts for the same issue on every `--resume --from-stage` invocation — the second restore silently no-ops due to the no-clobber guard but the git operations both fire. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:2921; fix: code)

red-team lens, medium: The latest-symlink auto-issue-discovery block (lines 1827-1836) reads the issue number from `$state_dir/latest/pipeline-state.json` and sets `issue` from it when no `--issue`/`--goal` was supplied; this happens BEFORE the ZBUILD_STATE_FILE vs. --issue cross-check at line 1878, but the cross-check only fires when `ZBUILD_STATE_FILE` is set — a crafted or stale `latest` symlink pointing at a different issue's state silently routes the run under the wrong issue identity with no mismatch error. (core/pipeline/runner.sh:1827; fix: code)
